lesson_scope: Operations on complex numbers in Cartesian form, complex conjugates, division by multiplying by the conjugate, linear equations in z and z*, and simultaneous linear complex equations.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct division and rationalisation of a complex fraction.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rationalisation of a complex denominator using its complex conjugate.

hints: Multiply both the numerator and denominator by the complex conjugate of $2 - 3\mathrm{i}$, which is $2 + 3\mathrm{i}$.
Expand the numerator $(7 + 4\mathrm{i})(2 + 3\mathrm{i})$ and denominator $(2 - 3\mathrm{i})(2 + 3\mathrm{i}) = 2^2 + 3^2 = 13$ using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$.
Separate into real and imaginary fractions: $\frac{2}{13} + \frac{29}{13}\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator, $2 + 3\mathrm{i}$:
$$z = \frac{7 + 4\mathrm{i}}{2 - 3\mathrm{i}} = \frac{(7 + 4\mathrm{i})(2 + 3\mathrm{i})}{(2 - 3\mathrm{i})(2 + 3\mathrm{i})}$$

Expand the numerator and denominator using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$\text{Numerator} = 14 + 21\mathrm{i} + 8\mathrm{i} + 12\mathrm{i}^2 = 14 - 12 + 29\mathrm{i} = 2 + 29\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Denominator} = 2^2 - (3\mathrm{i})^2 = 4 - 9(-1) = 13$$

Express the result in the form $x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$z = \frac{2}{13} + \frac{29}{13}\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies numerator and denominator by $2 + 3\mathrm{i}$ and uses $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Complex division followed by finding the complex conjugate.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Simplification of a complex quotient followed by conjugate extraction.

hints: First express $w$ in Cartesian form $a + \mathrm{i}b$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by $1 - 2\mathrm{i}$.
Take the complex conjugate by negating the imaginary part: $w^* = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{7}{5}\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Simplify $w = \frac{3 - \mathrm{i}}{1 + 2\mathrm{i}}$ by multiplying by the conjugate $1 - 2\mathrm{i}$:
$$w = \frac{(3 - \mathrm{i})(1 - 2\mathrm{i})}{(1 + 2\mathrm{i})(1 - 2\mathrm{i})} = \frac{3 - 6\mathrm{i} - \mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i}^2}{1^2 + 2^2}$$

Use $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$ to obtain $w$ in Cartesian form:
$$w = \frac{3 - 7\mathrm{i} - 2}{5} = \frac{1 - 7\mathrm{i}}{5} = \frac{1}{5} - \frac{7}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

Find the complex conjugate $w^*$ by changing the sign of the imaginary component:
$$w^* = \frac{1}{5} + \frac{7}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Simplifies $w$ by multiplying numerator and denominator by $1 - 2\mathrm{i}$ using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Algebraic expansion of squares of a complex number and its conjugate.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Algebraic expansion and difference of conjugate powers.

hints: Expand $z^2 = (x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 - y^2 + 2\mathrm{i}xy$ and $(z^*)^2 = (x - \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 - y^2 - 2\mathrm{i}xy$.

walkthrough.text:
Expand $z^2$ and $(z^*)^2$ in terms of $x$ and $y$ using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$z^2 = (x + \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 + 2\mathrm{i}xy + \mathrm{i}^2 y^2 = (x^2 - y^2) + 2\mathrm{i}xy$$
$$(z^*)^2 = (x - \mathrm{i}y)^2 = x^2 - 2\mathrm{i}xy + \mathrm{i}^2 y^2 = (x^2 - y^2) - 2\mathrm{i}xy$$

Subtract the two expressions:
$$z^2 - (z^*)^2 = [(x^2 - y^2) + 2\mathrm{i}xy] - [(x^2 - y^2) - 2\mathrm{i}xy]$$
$$z^2 - (z^*)^2 = 2\mathrm{i}xy - (-2\mathrm{i}xy) = 4\mathrm{i}xy$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $z^2$ and $(z^*)^2$ in terms of $x$ and $y$ using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct linear equation with complex coefficients.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Linear complex equation rearrangement and division.

hints: Subtract $2 - 5\mathrm{i}$ from both sides to isolate $(3 + \mathrm{i})z$: $(3 + \mathrm{i})z = (8 + 7\mathrm{i}) - (2 - 5\mathrm{i}) = 6 + 12\mathrm{i}$.
Divide by $3 + \mathrm{i}$ and multiply numerator and denominator by $3 - \mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Rearrange the equation to isolate the term containing $z$:
$$(3 + \mathrm{i})z = (8 + 7\mathrm{i}) - (2 - 5\mathrm{i}) = (8 - 2) + \mathrm{i}(7 - (-5)) = 6 + 12\mathrm{i}$$

Divide by $3 + \mathrm{i}$ and multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate $3 - \mathrm{i}$:
$$z = \frac{6 + 12\mathrm{i}}{3 + \mathrm{i}} = \frac{(6 + 12\mathrm{i})(3 - \mathrm{i})}{(3 + \mathrm{i})(3 - \mathrm{i})}$$

Expand and simplify using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$z = \frac{18 - 6\mathrm{i} + 36\mathrm{i} - 12\mathrm{i}^2}{3^2 + 1^2} = \frac{18 + 30\mathrm{i} + 12}{10} = \frac{30 + 30\mathrm{i}}{10} = 3 + 3\mathrm{i}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Linear equation coupling z and its conjugate z*.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separation of real and imaginary parts from a linear combination of z and z*.

hints: Equate real parts $5x = 15 \implies x = 3$ and imaginary parts $-y = -4 \implies y = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ into the given equation:
$$2(x + \mathrm{i}y) + 3(x - \mathrm{i}y) = 15 - 4\mathrm{i}$$

Expand and group real and imaginary terms:
$$(2x + 3x) + \mathrm{i}(2y - 3y) = 15 - 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$5x - \mathrm{i}y = 15 - 4\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real parts and imaginary parts:
$$\text{Real: } 5x = 15 \implies x = 3$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } -y = -4 \implies y = 4$$
Conclusion: $x = 3$ and $y = 4$.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ to obtain $5x - \mathrm{i}y = 15 - 4\mathrm{i}$.
Equates real and imaginary parts to form $5x = 15$ and $-y = -4$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Rational complex equation involving cross-multiplication.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cross-multiplication and solving a fractional complex equation.

walkthrough.text:
Cross-multiply by $z - 2$ to clear the denominator:
$$z + 4\mathrm{i} = (1 + 2\mathrm{i})(z - 2)$$

Expand the right-hand side:
$$z + 4\mathrm{i} = (1 + 2\mathrm{i})z - 2(1 + 2\mathrm{i}) = (1 + 2\mathrm{i})z - 2 - 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$2 + 8\mathrm{i} = (1 + 2\mathrm{i})z - z$$
$$2\mathrm{i}z = 2 + 8\mathrm{i}$$

Divide by $2\mathrm{i}$ and evaluate using $\frac{1}{\mathrm{i}} = -\mathrm{i}$:
$$z = \frac{2 + 8\mathrm{i}}{2\mathrm{i}} = \frac{1 + 4\mathrm{i}}{\mathrm{i}} = (1 + 4\mathrm{i})(-\mathrm{i}) = -\mathrm{i} - 4\mathrm{i}^2 = 4 - \mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands and groups $z$ terms to obtain $2\mathrm{i}z = 2 + 8\mathrm{i}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Linear complex equation with conjugate leading to a 2x2 system.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Substituting z = x + iy and z* = x - iy to formulate simultaneous linear equations.

hints: Collect real terms $(2x + 4y)$ and imaginary terms $\mathrm{i}(2x + 2y)$, then equate to $4 + 10\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ into the given equation:
$$(2 - \mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) + 3\mathrm{i}(x - \mathrm{i}y) = 4 + 10\mathrm{i}$$

Expand both products using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$(2x + 2\mathrm{i}y - \mathrm{i}x - \mathrm{i}^2 y) + (3\mathrm{i}x - 3\mathrm{i}^2 y) = 4 + 10\mathrm{i}$$
$$(2x + 2\mathrm{i}y - \mathrm{i}x + y) + (3\mathrm{i}x + 3y) = 4 + 10\mathrm{i}$$

Group the real and imaginary components on the left side:
$$(2x + 4y) + \mathrm{i}(2x + 2y) = 4 + 10\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real and imaginary parts to obtain the required equations:
$$\text{Real: } 2x + 4y = 4$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 2x + 2y = 10$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$, expands using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$, and collects real and imaginary parts.
Equates real and imaginary parts to $4$ and $10$ to obtain $2x + 4y = 4$ and $2x + 2y = 10$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving simultaneous linear equations to construct z.

hints: Subtract the second equation $2x + 2y = 10$ from the first $2x + 4y = 4$ to eliminate $x$.
Substitute $y = -3$ into $2x + 2(-3) = 10$ to find $x = 8$, and conclude $z = 8 - 3\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Subtract the two equations to eliminate $x$:
$$(2x + 4y) - (2x + 2y) = 4 - 10$$
$$2y = -6 \implies y = -3$$

Substitute $y = -3$ into $2x + 2y = 10$ to solve for $x$:
$$2x + 2(-3) = 10 \implies 2x - 6 = 10 \implies 2x = 16 \implies x = 8$$

State the complex number $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$:
$$z = 8 - 3\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Employs a valid elimination or substitution method on the simultaneous system.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Rational complex equation isolation and denominator rationalisation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Cross-multiplication and rearrangement to isolate z.

hints: Multiply both sides by $z - 3$ to get $z + 5\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i})(z - 3)$.
Group terms with $z$ on one side and constants on the other side: $(2 - \mathrm{i})z - z = 6 - 3\mathrm{i} + 5\mathrm{i} \implies z(1 - \mathrm{i}) = 6 + 2\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Cross-multiply both sides by $z - 3$:
$$z + 5\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i})(z - 3)$$

Expand the right-hand side using distributive law:
$$z + 5\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i})z - 3(2 - \mathrm{i}) = (2 - \mathrm{i})z - 6 + 3\mathrm{i}$$

Collect terms containing $z$ on one side and constant terms on the other:
$$6 - 3\mathrm{i} + 5\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i})z - z$$
$$6 + 2\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i} - 1)z$$
$$z(1 - \mathrm{i}) = 6 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands the right-hand side using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$ to obtain $z + 5\mathrm{i} = (2 - \mathrm{i})z - 6 + 3\mathrm{i}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Evaluating complex quotient to obtain Cartesian coordinates.

hints: Expand numerator: $(6 + 2\mathrm{i})(1 + \mathrm{i}) = 6 + 8\mathrm{i} - 2 = 4 + 8\mathrm{i}$, and divide by $(1 - \mathrm{i})(1 + \mathrm{i}) = 2$ to get $z = 2 + 4\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate $z$ from part (a) and multiply by the conjugate $1 + \mathrm{i}$:
$$z = \frac{6 + 2\mathrm{i}}{1 - \mathrm{i}} = \frac{(6 + 2\mathrm{i})(1 + \mathrm{i})}{(1 - \mathrm{i})(1 + \mathrm{i})}$$

Expand the numerator and denominator using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$\text{Numerator} = 6 + 6\mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i}^2 = 6 + 8\mathrm{i} - 2 = 4 + 8\mathrm{i}$$
$$\text{Denominator} = 1^2 - \mathrm{i}^2 = 1 - (-1) = 2$$

Divide each term by 2 to state $z$ in Cartesian form:
$$z = \frac{4 + 8\mathrm{i}}{2} = 2 + 4\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Multiplies numerator and denominator of $\frac{6 + 2\mathrm{i}}{1 - \mathrm{i}}$ by $1 + \mathrm{i}$.
Expands numerator to $4 + 8\mathrm{i}$ and denominator to $2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Rigorous proof of conjugate product law and power evaluation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Algebraic proof of conjugate product identity (uw)* = u*w*.

hints: Write $u = a + \mathrm{i}b$ and $w = c + \mathrm{i}d$. Expand the product $uw = (ac - bd) + \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$.
Take the conjugate of $uw$: $(uw)^* = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$.
Separately expand $u^* w^* = (a - \mathrm{i}b)(c - \mathrm{i}d) = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$ and compare expressions.

walkthrough.text:
Compute the product $uw$ and its complex conjugate:
$$uw = (a + \mathrm{i}b)(c + \mathrm{i}d) = ac + \mathrm{i}ad + \mathrm{i}bc + \mathrm{i}^2 bd = (ac - bd) + \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$$
$$(uw)^* = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$$

Compute the product of the individual conjugates $u^* = a - \mathrm{i}b$ and $w^* = c - \mathrm{i}d$:
$$u^* w^* = (a - \mathrm{i}b)(c - \mathrm{i}d) = ac - \mathrm{i}ad - \mathrm{i}bc + \mathrm{i}^2 bd = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$$

Conclude the proof by observing that both sides yield identical algebraic expressions:
$$(uw)^* = u^* w^* = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $uw$ and correctly states the complex conjugate $(uw)^* = (ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$.
Completes the proof showing both sides equal $(ac - bd) - \mathrm{i}(ad + bc)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Extending conjugate product law to integer powers.

hints: Apply the product rule $(z_1 z_2)^* = z_1^* z_2^*$ with $z_1 = z^2$ and $z_2 = z$ to deduce $(z^3)^* = (z^*)^3$.

walkthrough.text:
Deduce $(z^3)^* = (z^*)^3$ by repeated application of the product property from part (a):
$$(z^2)^* = (z \cdot z)^* = z^* \cdot z^* = (z^*)^2$$
$$(z^3)^* = (z^2 \cdot z)^* = (z^2)^* \cdot z^* = (z^*)^2 \cdot z^* = (z^*)^3$$

For $z = 1 + 2\mathrm{i}$, note that $z^* = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$ and compute $(z^*)^3$:
$$(z^*)^3 = (1 - 2\mathrm{i})^3 = 1^3 - 3(1^2)(2\mathrm{i}) + 3(1)(2\mathrm{i})^2 - (2\mathrm{i})^3$$

Simplify using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$ and $\mathrm{i}^3 = -\mathrm{i}$:
$$(z^*)^3 = 1 - 6\mathrm{i} + 3(-4) - 8(-\mathrm{i}) = 1 - 6\mathrm{i} - 12 + 8\mathrm{i} = -11 + 2\mathrm{i}$$
Therefore, $(z^3)^* = -11 + 2\mathrm{i}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Explains that $(z^3)^* = (z^*)^3$ using repeated application of $(uw)^* = u^* w^*$.
Expands $(1 - 2\mathrm{i})^3$ or $(1 + 2\mathrm{i})^3$ using binomial expansion and $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured core: Simultaneous linear system in real and imaginary parts with squared modulus.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Formulating simultaneous real equations from complex relation with conjugate.

hints: Subtract the terms: Real part is $(3x - 2y) - (x - y) = 2x - y$, Imaginary part is $(2x + 3y) - (-x - y) = 3x + 4y$, and equate to $4 + 28\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $w = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $w^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ into the equation:
$$(3 + 2\mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) - (1 - \mathrm{i})(x - \mathrm{i}y) = 4 + 28\mathrm{i}$$

Expand each product using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$(3 + 2\mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) = 3x + 3\mathrm{i}y + 2\mathrm{i}x - 2y = (3x - 2y) + \mathrm{i}(2x + 3y)$$
$$(1 - \mathrm{i})(x - \mathrm{i}y) = x - \mathrm{i}y - \mathrm{i}x + \mathrm{i}^2 y = (x - y) - \mathrm{i}(x + y)$$

Subtract the two expressions:
$$[(3x - 2y) - (x - y)] + \mathrm{i}[(2x + 3y) - (-(x + y))] = 4 + 28\mathrm{i}$$
$$(2x - y) + \mathrm{i}(3x + 4y) = 4 + 28\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real parts and imaginary parts:
$$\text{Real: } 2x - y = 4$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 3x + 4y = 28$$

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes $w = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $w^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ and expands products.
Applies $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$ and groups real and imaginary parts.
Equates real and imaginary parts to obtain $2x - y = 4$ and $3x + 4y = 28$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving simultaneous equations and finding modulus squared.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the simultaneous equations from part (a) by substitution:
$$y = 2x - 4$$
$$3x + 4(2x - 4) = 28$$
$$3x + 8x - 16 = 28$$
$$11x = 44 \implies x = 4$$

Find $y$ and state the complex number $w$:
$$y = 2(4) - 4 = 4$$
$$w = 4 + 4\mathrm{i}$$

Compute the squared modulus $|w|^2 = w w^*$:
$$|w|^2 = x^2 + y^2 = 4^2 + 4^2 = 16 + 16 = 32$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Simultaneous linear system in two complex unknowns u and w.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Simultaneous linear complex system elimination to isolate one variable.

hints: Substitute this into the second equation: $(1 - \mathrm{i})[(7 + 4\mathrm{i}) - 2\mathrm{i}w] + 3w = 8 - 7\mathrm{i}$.
Divide by $1 - 2\mathrm{i}$ and multiply by $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$ to obtain $w = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$.

walkthrough.text:
Isolate $u$ from the first equation:
$$u = 7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i}w$$

Substitute $u$ into the second equation:
$$(1 - \mathrm{i})(7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i}w) + 3w = 8 - 7\mathrm{i}$$

Expand and simplify the constant and $w$ coefficients using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$(1 - \mathrm{i})(7 + 4\mathrm{i}) = 7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 7\mathrm{i} - 4\mathrm{i}^2 = 11 - 3\mathrm{i}$$
$$-(1 - \mathrm{i})(2\mathrm{i})w = -(2\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i}^2)w = (-2 - 2\mathrm{i})w$$
$$(11 - 3\mathrm{i}) + (-2 - 2\mathrm{i})w + 3w = 8 - 7\mathrm{i}$$
$$(11 - 3\mathrm{i}) + (1 - 2\mathrm{i})w = 8 - 7\mathrm{i}$$

Isolate $w$ and rationalise the denominator:
$$(1 - 2\mathrm{i})w = (8 - 7\mathrm{i}) - (11 - 3\mathrm{i}) = -3 - 4\mathrm{i}$$
$$w = \frac{-3 - 4\mathrm{i}}{1 - 2\mathrm{i}} = \frac{(-3 - 4\mathrm{i})(1 + 2\mathrm{i})}{(1 - 2\mathrm{i})(1 + 2\mathrm{i})} = \frac{-3 - 6\mathrm{i} - 4\mathrm{i} + 8}{1 + 4} = \frac{5 - 10\mathrm{i}}{5} = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses $u = 7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i}w$ and substitutes into the second equation.
Expands $(1 - \mathrm{i})(7 + 4\mathrm{i}) = 11 - 3\mathrm{i}$ and collects $w$ terms to obtain $(1 - 2\mathrm{i})w$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Back-substitution and complex quotient evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Back-substitute $w = 1 - 2\mathrm{i}$ into the expression for $u$:
$$u = 7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i}(1 - 2\mathrm{i}) = 7 + 4\mathrm{i} - 2\mathrm{i} + 4\mathrm{i}^2 = 7 + 2\mathrm{i} - 4 = 3 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

Set up the quotient $\frac{u}{w}$ and multiply by the conjugate of $w$:
$$\frac{u}{w} = \frac{3 + 2\mathrm{i}}{1 - 2\mathrm{i}} = \frac{(3 + 2\mathrm{i})(1 + 2\mathrm{i})}{(1 - 2\mathrm{i})(1 + 2\mathrm{i})}$$

Expand and simplify using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$\frac{u}{w} = \frac{3 + 6\mathrm{i} + 2\mathrm{i} + 4\mathrm{i}^2}{1^2 + (-2)^2} = \frac{3 + 8\mathrm{i} - 4}{5} = \frac{-1 + 8\mathrm{i}}{5} = -\frac{1}{5} + \frac{8}{5}\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up quotient $\frac{3 + 2\mathrm{i}}{1 - 2\mathrm{i}}$ and multiplies by $1 + 2\mathrm{i}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Advanced conjugate transformation, solving system and unit modulus proof.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Substituting z = x + iy and finding conjugate of composite expression (z + a + ib)*.

hints: Note that $z + 3 - 2\mathrm{i} = (x + 3) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2)$, so its conjugate is $(x + 3) - \mathrm{i}(y - 2) = (x + 3) + \mathrm{i}(2 - y)$.
Sum the real parts $(x + 3) + (x - 2y) = 2x - 2y + 3$ and imaginary parts $(2 - y) + (2x + y) = 2x + 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Express $z + 3 - 2\mathrm{i}$ in Cartesian form and find its conjugate:
$$z + 3 - 2\mathrm{i} = (x + 3) + \mathrm{i}(y - 2)$$
$$(z + 3 - 2\mathrm{i})^* = (x + 3) - \mathrm{i}(y - 2) = (x + 3) + \mathrm{i}(2 - y)$$

Expand the second term $(1 + 2\mathrm{i})z$:
$$(1 + 2\mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) = x + \mathrm{i}y + 2\mathrm{i}x + 2\mathrm{i}^2 y = (x - 2y) + \mathrm{i}(2x + y)$$

Add the two expressions:
$$[(x + 3) + (x - 2y)] + \mathrm{i}[(2 - y) + (2x + y)] = 5 + 8\mathrm{i}$$
$$(2x - 2y + 3) + \mathrm{i}(2x + 2) = 5 + 8\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real and imaginary parts:
$$\text{Real: } 2x - 2y + 3 = 5 \implies 2x - 2y = 2$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } 2x + 2 = 8 \implies 2x = 6$$

ai_rubric.observable: Adds expressions to obtain real part $2x - 2y + 3$ and imaginary part $2x + 2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving for z, computing ratio with conjugate, and proving unit modulus.

walkthrough.text:
Solve the system from part (a):
$$2x = 6 \implies x = 3$$
$$2(3) - 2y = 2 \implies 6 - 2y = 2 \implies 2y = 4 \implies y = 2$$
$$z = 3 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

Prove that $|v| = 1$ using properties of moduli:
$$|v| = \left|\frac{z}{z^*}\right| = \frac{|z|}{|z^*|} = \frac{\sqrt{3^2 + 2^2}}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-2)^2}} = \frac{\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}} = 1$$

Express $v = \frac{z}{z^*}$ in Cartesian form $a + \mathrm{i}b$:
$$v = \frac{3 + 2\mathrm{i}}{3 - 2\mathrm{i}} = \frac{(3 + 2\mathrm{i})(3 + 2\mathrm{i})}{(3 - 2\mathrm{i})(3 + 2\mathrm{i})} = \frac{9 + 12\mathrm{i} + 4\mathrm{i}^2}{3^2 + 2^2} = \frac{5 + 12\mathrm{i}}{13} = \frac{5}{13} + \frac{12}{13}\mathrm{i}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Proves $|v| = 1$ using $|z|/|z^*| = 1$ or from algebraic evaluation.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured capstone: Parametric linear complex system, determinant singularity and modulus product.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Parametric linear complex equation decomposition into real and imaginary components.

hints: Add imaginary parts: $(2x + y) + (-x - ky) = x + (1 - k)y = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $z = x + \mathrm{i}y$ and $z^* = x - \mathrm{i}y$ into the given parametric equation:
$$(1 + 2\mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) + (k - \mathrm{i})(x - \mathrm{i}y) = 10 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

Expand each product using $\mathrm{i}^2 = -1$:
$$(1 + 2\mathrm{i})(x + \mathrm{i}y) = x + \mathrm{i}y + 2\mathrm{i}x + 2\mathrm{i}^2 y = (x - 2y) + \mathrm{i}(2x + y)$$
$$(k - \mathrm{i})(x - \mathrm{i}y) = kx - \mathrm{i}ky - \mathrm{i}x + \mathrm{i}^2 y = (kx - y) - \mathrm{i}(x + ky)$$

Group the real and imaginary parts together:
$$[(x - 2y) + (kx - y)] + \mathrm{i}[(2x + y) - (x + ky)] = 10 + 2\mathrm{i}$$
$$[(1 + k)x - 3y] + \mathrm{i}[x + (1 - k)y] = 10 + 2\mathrm{i}$$

Equate real parts and imaginary parts to obtain the required system:
$$\text{Real: } (1 + k)x - 3y = 10$$
$$\text{Imaginary: } x + (1 - k)y = 2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Collects real and imaginary parts on the left-hand side.
Equates to $10 + 2\mathrm{i}$ to obtain $(1 + k)x - 3y = 10$ and $x + (1 - k)y = 2$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding singularity conditions where a 2x2 linear system has no unique solution.

hints: A $2 \times 2$ system $a x + b y = p, c x + d y = q$ lacks a unique solution when its determinant $ad - bc = 0$.
Compute the determinant: $(1 + k)(1 - k) - (-3)(1) = (1 - k^2) + 3 = 4 - k^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the condition for the linear system in $x$ and $y$ to have no unique solution:
$$\begin{vmatrix} 1 + k & -3 \\ 1 & 1 - k \end{vmatrix} = 0$$

Solve for $k$:
$$k^2 = 4 \implies k = 2 \quad \text{or} \quad k = -2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Eliminates a variable or sets the determinant $(1 + k)(1 - k) - (-3)(1) = 0$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Solving system for specific parameter and computing product zz*.

hints: Substitute $k = 1$ into the system from part (a): $(1 + 1)x - 3y = 10 \implies 2x - 3y = 10$, and $x + (1 - 1)y = 2 \implies x = 2$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $k = 1$ into the simultaneous equations from part (a):
$$2x - 3y = 10$$
$$x + 0y = 2 \implies x = 2$$

Substitute $x = 2$ into the first equation to solve for $y$:
$$2(2) - 3y = 10 \implies 4 - 3y = 10 \implies -3y = 6 \implies y = -2$$
$$z = 2 - 2\mathrm{i}$$

Compute the product $z z^*$:
$$z z^* = (2 - 2\mathrm{i})(2 + 2\mathrm{i}) = 2^2 + (-2)^2 = 4 + 4 = 8$$
